answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a horizon, then slash it when independently sampled audits find fabricated work or collusion. Creating a thousand aliases no longer multiplies influence for free: each must tie up capital, and a detected fraud burns part of it. Random audit timing—the pulse—makes it harder to game checks, while an ember of reputation earned through verified tasks can grow only slowly, so fresh identities cannot instantly inherit trust.
